text_blocks.snippet: Interstitial lung diseases (ILDs) are a group of conditions that cause inflammation and scarring of the lungs' interstitial tissue, which is the space between the alveoli (air sacs) and blood vessels.

list.snippet: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF): The most common type of ILD, characterized by progressive scarring of the lungs.
Nonspecific interstitial pneumonia (NSIP): A type of ILD with unknown causes.
Hypersensitivity pneumonitis: An allergic reaction to inhaled substances, such as mold, bird droppings, or animal proteins.
Asbestosis: Scarring of the lungs caused by exposure to asbestos fibers.
